title: Using Protein Painting Mass Spectrometry to Define Ligand Receptor Interaction Sites
author: Alexandru Graur
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: competent cells (Thermo Scientific, catalog number: EC
Invitrogen alpha-bungarotoxin conjugates (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number: B
Disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS) (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number: A
Anhydrous DMSO (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number: D12345 )

steps.title: Transform and grow E. coli for Ac-AChBP expression
steps.instruction: Transform BL21(DE3) cells with recombinant Ac‑AChBP plasmid, inoculate 200 mL LB containing 100 µg/mL ampicillin, and grow overnight at 37 °C with shaking.

steps.title: Induce protein expression with IPTG
steps.instruction: Inoculate the overnight culture into 1.3 L LB at 37 °C, save 2 mL for a spectrophotometer blank, monitor OD600 after ~2 h; when OD600 reaches 0.2 add IPTG to a final 1 mM and incubate at 16 °C overnight.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the culture at 6,000×g for 15 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in fresh LB, repeat centrifugation, discard supernatant and keep the pellet (optional freeze at –80 °C up to 4 months).

steps.title: Lyse cells and collect fractions
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 50 mL lysis buffer with 500 µL 10 mg/mL DNase, 50 mg lysozyme, and one protease‑inhibitor tablet; sonicate; centrifuge 39,000×g for 45 min and collect the supernatant (lysis fraction). Then resuspend the remaining pellet in 50 mL Buffer A with one protease‑inhibitor tablet; sonicate; centrifuge 39,000×g for 30 min and collect the supernatant (load fraction) and the pellet (pellet fraction).

steps.title: Purify Ac-AChBP by Ni-NTA chromatography
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a Ni‑NTA IMAC column with Buffer A, wash with 30–50 mL Buffer A (save flowthrough as wash fraction), and elute protein with 15–20 mL Buffer B (elution fraction).

steps.title: Confirm expression by Bradford and SDS-PAGE
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration of pellet, lysis, load, wash, and elution fractions by Bradford assay; load equal amounts on a 4–12 % Bis‑Tris gel, run with markers 60–10 kDa, stain with Coomassie, and verify a ~28 kDa Ac‑AChBP band.

steps.title: Concentrate protein and exchange buffer
steps.instruction: Concentrate the eluted protein using a 30 kDa Amicon Ultra filter for 15 min at 4 °C; discard flowthrough, refill the filter with final buffer to remove imidazole, and repeat the concentration step twice for complete buffer exchange.

steps.title: Prepare Ac-AChBP–ligand complexes
steps.instruction: Label Lo‑Bind 1.5 mL tubes for each condition; for each 65 µL sample combine 2.94 µL Ac‑AChBP, 1.60 µL α‑bungarotoxin, and 61.26 µL 1× PBS (or PBS only for control); incubate on a rotator at room temperature for 1 h at 20 rpm.

steps.title: Set up Sephadex spin columns
steps.instruction: Prepare one Sephadex G25 spin column per sample, give each a sharp downward shake, place the column (cap removed) in a 2 mL collection tube, add the resin from the cap back into the column, spin at 1,000×g for 1 min, then add 400 µL MilliQ water and keep at room temperature until the incubation in step 8 finishes.

steps.title: Apply diazo and NHS-ester dyes
steps.instruction: Add diazo and NHS‑ester dyes to painted samples and perform incubations as described.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µL diazo dye (5 mg/mL, freshly prepared from 1 mg in 200 µL PBS) to each painted sample; add 5 µL 1× PBS to each unpainted control; incubate 30 min at room temperature on a rotator.
Spin columns at 1,000×g for 1 min; add 5 µL 5 mg/mL NHS‑ester dye to painted samples and 5 µL DMSO to unpainted samples; incubate another 30 min at room temperature on a rotator.

steps.title: Pass samples through Sephadex and collect flowthrough
steps.instruction: Transfer samples through the Sephadex columns and retain the filtrate.

substeps.instruction: During the dye incubations, add 400 µL MilliQ water to each Sephadex column and centrifuge at 1,000×g for 2 min.
Remove the columns, place them in new labeled Lo‑Bind tubes ensuring no air pockets, then add the entire 75 µL sample to the column (add in the middle, avoid touching the resin).
Centrifuge at 1,000×g for 1 min, discard the columns, and keep the flowthrough for downstream processing.

steps.title: Denature, reduce and alkylate proteins
steps.instruction: Add 0.8 µL 250 µg/mL lysozyme stock, 25 µL 8 M urea (final 2 M, 100 µL total), and 1.1 µL 1 M DTT (final 10 mM, 101.1 µL total); incubate 30 min at 37 °C. Then add 12 µL iodoacetamide (final 50 mM, 113.1 µL total) and incubate in the dark at room temperature for at least 15 min.

steps.title: Digest proteins with trypsin
steps.instruction: Add 86.32 µL ultrapure water, 22 µL 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate, and 0.58 µL trypsin (use 0.5 µL minimum if calculated volume <0.5 µL) to reach a final volume of 222 µL (urea <1 M, 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, trypsin 1:10); digest overnight at 37 °C. Stop digestion by adding 5 µL acetic acid (~2 % final), then store samples at –20 °C.

steps.title: Desalt peptides on C-18 spin columns
steps.instruction: Thaw samples, add 75 µL sample buffer, centrifuge 1,000×g for 1 min; split each 150 µL sample into two 75 µL technical replicates (or load the whole volume) onto C‑18 spin columns following the manufacturer’s protocol, elute into clean 1.5 mL tubes, dry under nitrogen at 40 °C for ~10 min while monitoring to avoid loss, and store dried peptides at –20 °C until mass‑spectrometry analysis.
